title: At home
cando: say where you live, what is in your home and where things are

about.text: This lesson is about your home. You say where you live. You say where things are.
goals: Say: I live in a flat.
Name rooms: a kitchen, a bedroom.
Say where: It's under the table.
Use there is and there are.
Read a notice in your building.

chapters.title: Where do you live?
chapters.text:
Samir and Mei work together.
Samir asks Mei: Where do you live?
Mei says: I live in a flat.
She says what is in it.
Listen for the rooms.
A kitchen, a bedroom, a bathroom.

chapters.title: Where things are
chapters.text:
Small words say where.
In, on, under, next to.
The keys are on the table.
Say there is for one thing.
There is a kitchen.
Say there are for two or more.
There are two chairs.
My is for you. Our is for you and other people.

chapters.title: My flat
chapters.text:
Next, you read about Kwame's flat.
Then you read a building notice.
Then you write where your things are.

chapters.title: Draw my home
chapters.text:
Then you talk about your home.
A friend listens and draws it.
Say the rooms and where they are.
Is the picture right?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story.
Read it once for the story.
Then read it again. Answer the questions.

warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people live in a flat.

conversation.title: Where do you live?
conversation.setting: Samir and Mei work together. Mei has a new flat.
lines: I live in a flat. It's new!
No, it's small. There are three rooms.
Yes, and a bedroom and a bathroom.
Yes. My bed is under the window.
And you? Where do you live?
I live with my family. Our house has four bedrooms.

questions.why: Mei lives in a flat. She says: No, it's small.
Mei says: It's next to the bedroom.

questions.q: How many bedrooms are in Samir's house?
questions.why: Samir says: Our house has four bedrooms.

sound.title: th in bathroom
sound.explain: Put your tongue between your teeth. Blow out air. That is th. The second group has t, not th. Listen, then say each group.

sayIt.instructions: Say Mei's lines. Record yourself. Then listen back. Is your voice clear?

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation.
examples: My bed is under the window.
spot.question: Which words say where? When is it there is? When is it there are? Who is our for?
spot.answer: Next to and under say where. There is + one thing. There are + two or more. Our is for Samir and his family.

rules.title: Where things are
rule: Where is the bed? It's under the window.
in, on, under, next to: It's on the table.
There is + one: There is a kitchen.
There are + two or more: There are two chairs.
my = me. our = me and other people.
rules.mistake: Not: There is two chairs. Say: There are two chairs.

yourTurn.prompt: Where are your things now? Write three lines. Use in, on, under or next to.

text.title: My flat
text.type: A short text and a notice
text.body:
MY FLAT
by Kwame
I live with my brother.
Our flat is small.
There are two bedrooms.
There is a kitchen and a bathroom.
My bedroom has a big window.
The lift is next to our door.

HILL VIEW FLATS
NOTICE
No lift today. Please use the stairs.
Do not put rubbish on the stairs.
Please close the front door.

gist.why: It says: Hill View Flats. Notice.

detail.why: Kwame says: There are two bedrooms.
Kwame says: I live with my brother.
The lift is next to our door.
No lift today. Please use the stairs.

items.meaning: You open it. Then you go in.
You look out of it. Light comes in.
items.example: My bedroom has a big window.

items.meaning: You go up and down them.
items.example: The stairs are next to the lift.

items.meaning: A small room. It takes you up and down.
Paper and food you do not want.

write.task: Write four lines. Where are your things at home? Copy the model. Change the words.
checklist: Each line says where a thing is.
I use in, on, under or next to.
I use is and are right.

card.title: Draw my home
card.situation: Your friend wants to see your home. There is no photo. Your friend has a pen and paper.
card.goal: Say the rooms and where they are. Say where three things are. Your friend draws your home.

phrases: There is a kitchen and a bathroom.
The kitchen is next to the door.
The bed is under the window.
The table is in the kitchen.
prepare.notes: Draw your home first. Then write the rooms and three things.

doIt.liveClass: Tell your teacher about your home. Your teacher draws it. Is the picture right? Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: I talk about my home. You listen. Ask me: How many rooms? Where is the kitchen? Then say my home back to me. Use very simple English.

quiz.q: I live ___ a house with my family.
quiz.why: Say: I live in a house.
The kitchen is the room for food.

quiz.q: Where ___ the lift? It's next to the stairs.
No lift today. Please use the ___ .
quiz.why: No lift, so you use the stairs.
Old starts with o: an old flat.

quiz.q: This is my sister. ___ name is Priya.
quiz.why: A sister is a woman, so her.
You can count rooms, so how many.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the conversation in pairs. Then learners ask each other: Where do you live? Is there a kitchen?
Day 2: the task. Each learner describes their home and you draw it on the board. Check the drawing together, then a learner draws while you describe.
Day 3: talk about the book. Then hide a key in the room; learners ask Where is it? and answer with in, on, under and next to.
